event.title: Transforming Communities & Culture Through AI – TEDxBradleyUniversity
event.description: TEDxBradley University invites the Central Illinois community to explore how artificial intelligence is reshaping the way we connect, compete, collaborate, and create. From classrooms to boardrooms and even digital arenas, AI is redefining how communities form and thrive. Register Here Ideas Change Everything! Ideas pave the road for creative and transformative thinking to tackle today’s complex societal challenges and design solutions that address tomorrow’s societal realities. Thought leaders will deliver compelling, idea-driven talks that spark collaboration, promote ethical AI use, and empower individuals to create networks and neighborhoods. Join us to discover how AI can transcend divides, amplify human connections, and help build resilient communities.

event.title: James Jaxxa “What We Make Sacred” (Start)
event.description: James Jaxxa “What We Make Sacred” Exhibition Hartman Gallery, Bradley University Oct. 1st – Dec 15th Opening Reception Oct. 1st 6:30-8:00 pm Visual Voices Lecture Caterpillar Global Communications Center Room 126 Oct. 1st 5:00-6:00pm Bio James Jaxxa’s multi-faceted practice explores themes of memory, desire, vulnerability, community and pleasure through the creation of bedazzling personal reliquaries and cathartic shrines. His work is influenced from growing up nomadically in a military family, Catholic iconography and queer culture. He received his MFA from the School of Visual Arts, his BS from Michigan State University and completed post-baccalaureate work at School of the Art Institute of Chicago and Rhode Island School of Design. He has attended residencies at Barac (Mannheim, Germany), Salzburg International Summer Academy (Salzburg, Austria), R.A.R.O. (Barcelona, Spain), Berlin Art Institute (Berlin, Germany) and others. Jaxxa’s work has been shown in exhibitions across the United States and internationally including those at Terrain Biennial, New York Public Library, The LGBT Center in New York, University of Nevada, Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Seattle Art Museum, Bellevue Art Museum and numerous other institutions and galleries. His public artwork, Potential Connections was installed for the inauguration of Seattle’s Link Light Rail system. Jaxxa has been included in publications by The New York Times, Visual AIDS, New York Public Library and The Seattle Times. He was awarded an Artists Space Independent Project Grant. Jaxxa is a founding member of I Found U, an international group of artists working across different materials and mediums, committed to discussion and collaboration on environmental, sociological and economic concerns. He lives and works in New York City. What The Nights Left Behind, archival pigment prints, mixed media on wood panel, 36 x 36 x 2-3/16 inches: Somewhere Between Heaven and The Dance Floor, mixed media on wood panel, 36 x 46 x 2-1/8 inches:

event.title: Broadway Comes To Bradley II
event.description: Broadway Comes To Bradley II October, 3, 2026 at 7:30pm in the Meyer Jacobs Theatre For one night only… Broadway performer and Bradley University Theatre Arts Performance alum Morgan Siobhan Green, along with award-winning composer and lyricist Joe Iconis, are coming to Bradley! After last year’s triumphant Broadway Comes to Bradley, in which Morgan performed alongside Tony and Pulitzer Prize winner Michael R. Jackson (A Strange Loop), we are thrilled to bring Morgan back again, along with another of her dear friends from the world of Broadway: composer and lyricist Joe Iconis. Morgan was one of Bradley Theatre’s all-time best actors, excelled on BU’s Speech Team, and performed in Broadway’s Be More Chill and in the US National Tour of the smash-hit Broadway musical Hadestown. Joe’s highly acclaimed musical Be More Chill was nominated for numerous Tony, Drama Desk, and Outer Critics Circle awards. This prolific artist has also written the music and lyrics for the musicals Broadway Bounty Hunter and Love in Hate Nation, and developed the musicals The Untitled Hunter S. Thompson Musical and Punk Rock Girl, among many other projects. Morgan and Joe, along with Bradley’s Theatre Arts and Music students, will perform an evening of original music that is sure to delight and inspire. Tickets can be purchased in-person at the Hartmann Center box office, or online. Please join us for Broadway Comes to Bradley II – an exciting evening of music and fun!

event.title: Zootober
event.description: Halloween gets a little WILD at Zootober! Each weekend, Peoria Zoo comes alive with glowing lights, creepy creatures, surprising characters, and plenty of Halloween fun for the whole family. Explore the Zoo as you make your way through immersive Halloween scenes featuring lifelike animatronics, dazzling light displays, and live actors waiting around the corner. Stroll along spooky trails and displays while collecting candy at stops along the way. Grab a spooky snack or themed drink, stop for a Halloween photo op, enjoy hands-on activities, and see what strange new creatures you might encounter. Event hours: 5:30 – 9:00 PM Last ticket sales: 8:00 PM Ticket Information: Tickets can be purchased online or in-person at the Zoo or Noble Center Online Sales: $14 / person (includes any online fees) In-Person Sales: $17 / person Members: Get 10% off with discount code! Tickets are required for guests ages 2 and up Zootober uses timed entry tickets at 5:30, 6:00, 6:30, 7:00, 7:30, and 8:00 p.m. Your ticketed time is simply your entry window. Once you’re inside, you’re welcome to stay and enjoy Zootober until the event closes! Please note, all ticket purchases are final. There will be no animals on exhibit during Zootober, but the Zoo will be crawling with eerie “creatures”! Click here for more information about the event, including Saturday night entertainment, Wildly Accessible Day, Glen Oak Express train schedule and more! Whether you’re looking for Halloween thrills, a night of family fun, or just an excuse to put on a costume and wander through the Zoo after dark, Zootober is ready to get a little spooky.

event.title: Henry IV, Part 1 by William Shakespeare
event.description: Henry IV, Part 1 by William Shakespeare November 5 – 15, 2026 in the O’Sullivan Studio Theatre Directed by Debbie Alley Bradley returns to the O’Sullivan Studio Theatre for a mainstage production for the first time since 2017 with Henry IV, Part One, a Shakespearean masterpiece about King Henry IV’s struggle with rebellious nobles (particularly Henry “Hotspur” Percy), while his son, Prince Hal, navigates a wild life with the roguish Falstaff, before proving his worth. This history play, written around 1597, covers the period from late 1402 to mid-1403 and explores themes of honor, rebellion, and father-son relationships, contrasting the king’s disappointment in Hal with his envy of Hotspur’s gallantry. The production will be guest-directed by Debbie Alley, a nationally respected theatre artist and educator. Purchase tickets

He received his MFA from the School of Visual Arts, his BS from Michigan State University and completed post-baccalaureate work at School of the Art Institute of Chicago and Rhode Island School of Design. He has attended residencies at Barac (Mannheim, Germany), Salzburg International Summer Academy (Salzburg, Austria), R.A.R.O. (Barcelona, Spain), Berlin Art Institute (Berlin, Germany) and others. Jaxxa’s work has been shown in exhibitions across the United States and internationally including those at Terrain Biennial, New York Public Library, The LGBT Center in New York, University of Nevada, Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Seattle Art Museum, Bellevue Art Museum and numerous other institutions and galleries. His public artwork, Potential Connections was installed for the inauguration of Seattle’s Link Light Rail system. Jaxxa has been included in publications by The New York Times, Visual AIDS, New York Public Library and The Seattle Times. He was awarded an Artists Space Independent Project Grant. Jaxxa is a founding member of I Found U, an international group of artists working across different materials and mediums, committed to discussion and collaboration on environmental, sociological and economic concerns. He lives and works in New York City.
